rules.name: SQL Injection
rules.description: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command can allow attacker-controlled input to modify a database query.
rules.guidance: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements instead of building SQL queries through string concatenation.

rules.name: OS Command Injection
rules.description: External input is incorporated into an operating system command without sufficient validation or neutralization.
rules.guidance: Avoid shell execution with untrusted input. Prefer safe APIs and strict allowlists for required arguments.

rules.name: Path Traversal
rules.description: External input can influence a filesystem path and potentially allow access outside the intended directory.
rules.guidance: Validate paths, restrict access to an intended base directory, and safely resolve and verify the resulting path.

rules.name: Server-Side Request Forgery
rules.description: A server makes network requests using attacker-controlled input, potentially allowing access to internal or restricted resources.
rules.guidance: Validate and restrict destination URLs, use allowlists where possible, and block access to internal network ranges.

rules.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
rules.description: Untrusted or attacker-controlled serialized data is deserialized in an unsafe way.
rules.guidance: Avoid deserializing untrusted data when possible. Use safe serialization formats and validate data before processing.

rules.name: Improper Authentication
rules.description: The application does not properly verify the identity of a user or system before granting access.
rules.guidance: Use established authentication mechanisms and ensure identity verification occurs before protected operations.

rules.name: Missing Authorization
rules.description: The application does not properly verify whether an authenticated user is authorized to perform an operation.
rules.guidance: Perform server-side authorization checks for every protected resource and sensitive operation.

rules.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery
rules.description: A web application accepts state-changing requests without adequately verifying that the request was intentionally made by the authenticated user.
rules.guidance: Use CSRF tokens or equivalent protections and configure appropriate cookie security attributes.

rules.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information
rules.description: The application exposes sensitive information through responses, logs, errors, or other externally accessible outputs.
rules.guidance: Return only necessary information and avoid exposing secrets, internal paths, stack traces, or sensitive application details.

rules.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
rules.description: An application consumes excessive resources because input size, processing time, or resource usage is not adequately controlled.
rules.guidance: Apply appropriate input limits, timeouts, quotas, pagination, and resource controls.
